title: Art as Selective Re-creation
summary: Art as a selective re-creation of reality according to metaphysical value-judgments.

lessons.title: What Art Is
lessons.objective: State the definition of art as a selective re-creation of reality according to metaphysical value-judgments.

exercises.prompt: On this account, what is art?

choices.text: A selective re-creation of reality according to metaphysical value-judgments
An unedited copy of whatever happens to be in front of the artist
A private mood with no tie to reality
Any object someone calls useful

feedback.note: The unit’s definition has three parts: selection, a re-creation of reality, and metaphysical value-judgments.

exercises.prompt: Which word names the thing art re-creates?

choices.text: Reality
A wish that replaces facts
A public vote
A fashion label by itself

feedback.note: Art re-creates reality. It does not start from nothing and it does not treat wishes as a substitute for what is.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the definition to what it names.

pairs.left: Selective
pairs.right: The artist chooses what to include

pairs.left: Re-creation of reality
pairs.right: The work presents reality again, shaped by that choice

pairs.left: Metaphysical value-judgments
pairs.right: The standard that guides the choice

feedback.note: Drop any one of the three parts and the definition is no longer the one this unit teaches.

exercises.prompt: Complete the definition.

feedback.note: Selective names the choice. Reality names what is re-created.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition in order.

feedback.note: The order is the claim: art, then selective re-creation, then of reality, then the standard of selection.

exercises.prompt: What does the definition rule out as a full account of art?

choices.text: An unselective dump of everything the artist notices
A chosen presentation of reality
A work shaped by a view of existence
Selection guided by what the artist takes as fundamental

feedback.note: If nothing is selected, the work is not the kind of re-creation the definition names.

exercises.prompt: Whose judgments set the selection, on this definition?

choices.text: The artist’s metaphysical value-judgments
Whatever a crowd happens to like that day
No one’s; selection needs no standard
Only the price of the materials

feedback.note: The according-to clause names the artist’s metaphysical value-judgments as the standard of what is chosen.

exercises.prompt: A metaphysical value-judgment, in this definition, is a judgment about what?

choices.text: What is fundamental about man and existence
Only the market price of the work
Only spelling and grammar
Only the weather on the day it was made

feedback.note: Metaphysical here means a judgment about the nature of existence, not a tip about technique or sales.

exercises.prompt: Match each mistaken slogan to the part of the definition it drops.

pairs.left: Art is whatever spills out, unchosen
Art invents a world with no reality in it
Art chooses, but by no view of existence

feedback.note: Each slogan keeps some words of the definition and throws away one essential part.

exercises.prompt: Name the standard that guides the selection.

parts.text: The selection follows the artist’s metaphysical

feedback.note: Value-judgments of a metaphysical kind are the according-to clause of the definition.

lessons.title: What Selective Means
lessons.objective: Explain that the artist includes, omits, and stresses aspects of reality rather than recording everything.

exercises.prompt: What does selective mean in this definition?

choices.text: The artist chooses which aspects to include, omit, and stress
The artist must include every fact equally
The artist must avoid anything real
The work is finished by chance

feedback.note: Selection is a choice among aspects of reality, not a refusal of reality and not a dump of all of it.

exercises.prompt: Leaving something out of a work is compatible with the definition when the omission is what?

choices.text: Part of a deliberate selection
Proof that reality was never the subject
Always a failure to copy the whole world
Forbidden by the word re-creation

feedback.note: Re-creation is selective, so omission is how the artist isolates what the work is about.

exercises.prompt: Match each act of selection to what it does.

pairs.left: Include
pairs.right: Puts an aspect into the work

pairs.left: Omit
pairs.right: Leaves an aspect out on purpose

pairs.left: Stress
pairs.right: Makes one included aspect stand out

feedback.note: Include, omit, and stress are three ways the same selection is carried out.

exercises.prompt: Fill in what the artist does not do.

parts.text: A selective re-creation is not an

feedback.note: If every detail stayed in at equal weight, nothing would have been selected.

exercises.prompt: Put the idea of selection in order.

feedback.note: Choice among real aspects is selection. Total inclusion and total rejection of reality are not.

exercises.prompt: Two painters look at the same city. One stresses human achievement and omits decay. The other does the reverse. What does the definition say they differ in?

choices.text: What each selects as worth presenting
Whether a city can exist
Whether either of them has eyes
Nothing; the same subject forces the same work

feedback.note: The same reality can be re-created under different selections. That is what selective allows.

exercises.prompt: Stressing one feature means what?

choices.text: Giving that feature more weight than other included features
Erasing the feature so it cannot be seen
Replacing reality with a feature that could not exist
Listing every feature at the same size

feedback.note: Stress is still selection inside what was included. It is emphasis, not a denial that the feature is real.

exercises.prompt: Which job is not what selective means?

choices.text: Taking a census of every fact with no emphasis
Omitting what does not serve the work
Keeping what the artist judges essential
Ranking some aspects above others

feedback.note: A census tries not to select. Art, on this definition, must select.

exercises.prompt: Match the practice to selective or not selective.

pairs.left: Isolating one human choice as the center of a story
Keeping every street noise because it occurred
Cutting a scene that does not bear on the theme

feedback.note: Selection is purposeful inclusion and omission. Recording an event only because it happened is not that.

exercises.prompt: Name the three moves of selection.

feedback.note: Include, omit, and stress are the concrete meaning of selective in this unit.

lessons.title: Re-creation, Not a Dump or a Fantasy
lessons.objective: Distinguish a re-creation of reality from an unselective record and from a presentation cut off from reality.

exercises.prompt: What does re-creation add beyond a bare record?

choices.text: Reality is presented again in a form the artist has made
Reality is dropped so nothing recognizable remains
The work must be indistinguishable from the original scene
The work must function only as a news bulletin

feedback.note: Re-creation keeps reality as the subject and presents it in a made work, not as a raw transcript.

exercises.prompt: A work that presents nothing the audience can tie back to reality fails which part of the definition?

choices.text: Re-creation of reality
Only the word selective, while reality stays irrelevant
None; the definition allows a total break with reality
Only the price of admission

feedback.note: Of reality is not optional. A presentation with no hold on reality is not this kind of re-creation.

exercises.prompt: Match each product to the right description.

pairs.left: A novel that condenses how people face choices
A log that lists every minute with no emphasis
Marks that are offered as referring to nothing real

feedback.note: Only the first item both selects and re-creates reality. The log does not select. The marks do not re-create reality.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

parts.text: Art re-creates reality; it does not
reality with a world that has no tie to it.

feedback.note: Re-creation presents reality again. Replacing reality is a different claim and not this definition.

exercises.prompt: Build the contrast in one line.

tokens.text: in a form the artist made

feedback.note: Made form plus a hold on reality is re-creation. A raw transcript and a break with facts are the two misses.

exercises.prompt: Why is an exact duplicate of one afternoon, detail for detail and without emphasis, not yet the art this unit defines?

choices.text: Nothing has been selected
An afternoon is not part of reality
Any made object is banned
Only nonhuman subjects count as art

feedback.note: The duplicate stays with reality but skips selection, so it is not a selective re-creation.

exercises.prompt: A story about people who choose is still a re-creation of reality because choice is what?

choices.text: Something real about human beings, presented in a made story
Proof that the story has left reality
Something the definition forbids artists to show
Allowed only if the story is a newspaper

feedback.note: Showing real human capacities in a made plot is re-creation, not a departure from reality.

exercises.prompt: Which pair names the two errors this lesson contrasts with re-creation?

choices.text: An unselective record, and a presentation cut off from reality
Using color, and using words
Practice, and more practice
A frame, and a pedestal

feedback.note: One error keeps every fact and selects nothing. The other selects, or gestures, without re-creating reality.

exercises.prompt: Name the subject that is presented again.

feedback.note: Presented again is the plain sense of re-creation in this unit.

exercises.prompt: Match the phrase to the error or the definition.

pairs.left: Everything that happened, in the order it happened, with no point
A world offered as having no connection to what exists
Chosen essentials of reality, presented in a work

feedback.note: The third line is the one that belongs in the definition of art used here.

lessons.title: Metaphysical Value-Judgments
lessons.objective: Identify metaphysical value-judgments as the artist’s fundamental appraisal of man and existence, and as the standard of selection.

exercises.prompt: In this definition, what are metaphysical value-judgments?

choices.text: The artist’s fundamental appraisal of man and of existence
Tips about brushes, meters, or camera settings
A guess about what will sell this week
A tally of how many people clapped

feedback.note: Metaphysical value-judgments appraise what existence and human life are like at the most basic level. They are not craft tips or sales forecasts.

exercises.prompt: How do those judgments enter the work, on this account?

choices.text: They guide what the artist selects to re-create
They appear only as a footnote after the work is done
They are kept out so selection can be standardless
They replace reality as the subject of the work

feedback.note: The according-to clause means the judgments are the standard of selection, not a substitute for reality and not an afterthought.

exercises.prompt: Match each judgment to the kind of selection it would guide.

pairs.left: Human effort can succeed
Human life is futile
pairs.right: Stress defeat as the essential outcome

pairs.left: Only chance matters
pairs.right: Treat choice as pointless and stress accident

feedback.note: Different appraisals of existence lead the artist to include, omit, and stress different aspects of the same reality.

exercises.prompt: Complete the according-to clause.

feedback.note: The standard is a metaphysical appraisal, not a shopping rank or a list of tools.

exercises.prompt: Build the role of the judgments.

feedback.note: They standardize selection. They do not cancel the subject or make selection unnecessary.

exercises.prompt: Why does the definition call the judgments metaphysical rather than only moral or technical?

choices.text: They concern what is fundamental about existence, not only a local rule of craft
They concern only which pigment is cheaper
The word adds nothing and can be dropped
They are courtroom verdicts about a particular case

feedback.note: Metaphysical marks the scope: an appraisal of existence and of man’s place in it, which then directs selection.

exercises.prompt: Can two artists re-create reality and still produce profoundly different works?

choices.text: Yes, if their metaphysical value-judgments differ
No, because reality allows only one work
No, because value-judgments are banned from art
No, unless they use different alphabets

feedback.note: Same reality, different fundamental appraisals, different selections. That is built into the definition.

exercises.prompt: Which item is not a metaphysical value-judgment in the sense this unit uses?

choices.text: This brush holds more paint than that one
A human being is capable of purpose
The world is open to understanding
Success is an illusion

feedback.note: A brush comparison is technical. The other three appraise man or existence and could guide what a work stresses.

exercises.prompt: Match each label to its role in the definition.

pairs.left: Reality
Metaphysical value-judgments
Selective re-creation
pairs.right: The kind of act art is

feedback.note: Subject, standard, and act are three different jobs. The judgments are the standard, not the subject.

exercises.prompt: Say what the judgments appraise.

feedback.note: Man and existence are the subject of the appraisal. Prices and tools are not what metaphysical means here.

lessons.title: One Claim, Three Parts
lessons.objective: Apply the full definition, keeping selection, re-creation of reality, and metaphysical value-judgments together.

exercises.prompt: A poster stacks slogans to push a vote and never presents a concrete slice of reality. What does this unit’s definition withhold from it?

choices.text: The status of a selective re-creation of reality
The right to use words at all
The fact that it is printed on paper
The possibility that its author has any aim

feedback.note: An aim is not enough. The definition requires a selective re-creation of reality, not a stack of slogans standing in for that.

exercises.prompt: A photograph is framed, timed, and lit so that one human action stands as essential, expressing the photographer’s view that people can direct their lives. Which reading fits the definition?

choices.text: It can be a selective re-creation guided by a metaphysical value-judgment
A camera image can never be selective
A real street cannot be the subject of art
A view of human life is irrelevant to what was framed

feedback.note: Framing, timing, and emphasis are selection. The view of human life is the kind of judgment the definition names as the standard.

exercises.prompt: Match each work-sketch to the part it satisfies or misses.

pairs.left: Every fact kept, none stressed, no appraisal in charge
A chosen scene of purposeful work, shaped by the view that effort matters
Shapes offered as meaning nothing about reality

feedback.note: Only the middle sketch selects, re-creates reality, and does so according to a metaphysical value-judgment.

exercises.prompt: Hold the three requirements in one line.

feedback.note: All three must stay in the claim. Fashion or chance is not a stand-in for either missing word.

exercises.prompt: Build the full claim.

feedback.note: The sentence keeps the act, the subject, and the standard. The extra tokens are the errors this unit rejects.

exercises.prompt: Someone says the definition is only about pretty objects. What is wrong with that reading?

choices.text: It never mentions selection, reality, or metaphysical value-judgments
Pretty is the word the definition uses for all three parts
A pretty object is automatically a re-creation of reality
Metaphysical judgments are the same thing as prettiness

feedback.note: Prettiness is not a part of this definition. The parts are selection, reality re-created, and metaphysical value-judgments.

exercises.prompt: If an artist’s selections embody the view that human beings are helpless, the work still counts as art on this definition when it does what?

choices.text: Selectively re-creates reality according to that metaphysical appraisal
Only if the appraisal says people are efficacious
Never, because a bleak appraisal voids the definition
Only if no selection took place

feedback.note: The definition names the kind of standard, a metaphysical value-judgment. It does not say only one such judgment yields art.

exercises.prompt: Which question applies this unit’s definition to a work?

choices.text: What of reality was selected, and by what view of existence?
What did the frame cost?
How many people walked past it?
Which brand of paint was used?

feedback.note: Cost, traffic, and brand do not answer whether the work is a selective re-creation according to metaphysical value-judgments.

exercises.prompt: Match the question to the part of the definition it checks.

pairs.left: What was included, omitted, and stressed?
Is reality presented again in the work?
What view of man and existence guided those choices?

feedback.note: Three questions, three parts. A full use of the definition asks all of them.

exercises.prompt: Close the unit’s claim.

parts.text: Art is a selective re-creation of reality according to metaphysical

feedback.note: That is the whole definition this unit teaches: selective re-creation of reality, standard set by metaphysical value-judgments.
